descriptors.label: Public FQDN
descriptors.description: Name users reach Vaultwarden by, for example vault.example.com; becomes DOMAIN, the nginx server name and the certificate name. It is also the WebAuthn/FIDO2 identity, so changing it later invalidates registered security keys. Empty derives it from the guest hostname and network.domain

descriptors.label: Time Zone
descriptors.description: IANA time zone for Vaultwarden, for example Europe/Prague; empty means UTC

descriptors.label: Organization Creators
descriptors.description: Comma-separated email addresses of the accounts allowed to create organizations. Empty means nobody can: set it to the first administrator's address for the initial bootstrap

descriptors.label: Admin Page Allowlist
descriptors.description: Space or comma separated addresses/CIDRs (management or VPN networks) allowed to reach /admin. Empty allows loopback only, i.e. an SSH tunnel. The admin token is required on top of this

descriptors.label: Admin Token Hash (argon2id)
descriptors.description: Optional argon2id PHC hash ($argon2id$v=19$...) of an admin token you hold, from 'vaultwarden-admin-token hash'. Empty (recommended) generates a token and shows it on the VM console once. Never put a plaintext token here

descriptors.label: HTTPS Allowlist
descriptors.description: Space or comma separated addresses/CIDRs allowed to reach HTTPS (and the HTTP redirect) through the guest firewall, for example the office and VPN ranges. Empty allows any source

descriptors.label: SSH Allowlist
descriptors.description: Space or comma separated management addresses/CIDRs allowed to SSH in. Empty keeps the base image's rule (any source). A wrong value locks SSH out; the console recovery account still works

descriptors.label: HTTP(S) Proxy
descriptors.description: Unauthenticated proxy (http://host:port, no user:password - a credential here would be readable by every local account) for the appliance's own outbound traffic: Ubuntu updates, image pulls for upgrades, website icons, push notifications and the OpenID Connect provider. Empty means connect directly

descriptors.label: Proxy Bypass List
descriptors.description: Comma-separated hosts, domains and CIDRs reached without the proxy. localhost is always bypassed

descriptors.label: TLS Certificate Chain (base64 PEM)
descriptors.description: Base64-encoded PEM chain, leaf first, from a public or company CA the clients trust. Bitwarden mobile and desktop apps refuse self-signed certificates, so this is needed for real use. Empty generates a self-signed certificate

descriptors.label: TLS Private Key (base64 PEM)
descriptors.description: Base64-encoded PEM private key matching the certificate above. Stored in the VM configuration in cleartext: prefer 'vaultwarden-tls install' after deployment, or clear this field once the VM has booted

descriptors.label: SMTP Server
descriptors.description: Mail relay for invitations, email verification and new-device notices. Empty leaves mail off: invited users can still register, but nothing is emailed and email verification is not enforced

descriptors.label: SMTP Port
descriptors.description: Empty uses the port matching the security mode: 587 for starttls, 465 for force_tls, 25 for off

descriptors.label: SMTP Security
descriptors.description: starttls (default), force_tls or off

descriptors.label: SMTP Sender Address
descriptors.description: From address, for example vaultwarden@example.com; required when an SMTP server is set

descriptors.label: SMTP Username
descriptors.description: Empty for an unauthenticated relay

descriptors.label: SMTP Password
descriptors.description: Stored on the appliance as a root-only file, never in the container environment. Clearing this field later keeps the stored password; vApp values are readable by vCenter users with access to the VM, so clear it once the VM has booted

descriptors.label: OpenID Connect Authority
descriptors.description: Optional, off by default. Issuer URL of a Keycloak realm or Microsoft Entra ID tenant, for example https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0. Users still need their master password to unlock their vault

descriptors.label: OpenID Connect Client ID
descriptors.description: Client id registered at the identity provider; SSO is enabled only when this and the authority are both set

descriptors.label: OpenID Connect Client Secret
descriptors.description: Required for SSO (Vaultwarden refuses to start with SSO enabled and no secret, so SSO stays off until all three are set). Stored on the appliance as a root-only file; clearing this field later keeps the stored secret

descriptors.label: OpenID Connect Scopes
descriptors.description: Space-separated scopes requested from the provider; empty means 'openid profile email offline_access'. offline_access is what makes the provider return a refresh token; without it an SSO session ends with the access token

descriptors.label: SSO Creates Accounts
descriptors.description: true lets a first SSO login create a Vaultwarden account for anyone the provider authenticates (control who that is at the provider, e.g. Entra ID 'assignment required'). Empty or false means an SSO login only works for an address that was invited first

descriptors.label: Accept Unknown Email Verification
descriptors.description: Set to true for Microsoft Entra ID, which sends no email_verified claim: without it Vaultwarden refuses every SSO login. Only safe with a provider where users cannot set their own email address, because an SSO login is linked to the existing local account with the same address
